name: Cauliflower
perishability: Highly perishable. 2–4 days at room temperature; curds yellow and spot quickly.
summary: A cool-season crop that India has bred to grow in heat. Varieties are grouped by the temperature at which they form a curd, so plains harvests run from September (early types) to March (snowball types). In the monsoon months only the hills supply, which is when prices peak.

key_numbers.label: Production
key_numbers.note: approx., recent years; second only to China

key_numbers.label: Price swing
key_numbers.note: between the winter glut and the monsoon peak in a typical year
key_numbers.src: CEDA / Agmarknet series on this site

global: India is the second-largest producer of cauliflower and broccoli after China. Almost all of it is eaten at home.

rows.hubs: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Assam, UP, Punjab, Himachal (summer), Maharashtra

belts.name: Bengal and Bihar plains
belts.note: Huge winter output; supplies East India and Delhi.

belts.name: Sonipat–Panipat
belts.note: Early and mid-season crops for Delhi.

belts.name: Kullu–Shimla–Solan
belts.note: Summer crop (Jun–Sep) when plains cannot grow it.

belts.name: Katrain (Kullu)
belts.note: ICAR-IARI station; source of snowball seed.

seasons.name: Early (plains)
seasons.note: Curds form at 20–27 °C; small curds, high prices.

lean_season: June–September: plains supply stops and the hills carry the market.

climate.v: Each maturity group needs its own temperature for curd formation: early 20–27 °C, mid 12–16 °C, snowball 10–16 °C.
Above ~30 °C curds turn ricey, leafy or loose; stress causes 'buttoning' (tiny premature curds).
Direct sun yellows curds; growers tie inner leaves over the curd (blanching).
Well-drained loam, pH 6.0–7.0. Boron shortage causes hollow stems and brown curds; molybdenum shortage causes 'whiptail'.

weather_risks.impact: Loose, ricey or leafy curds that fetch low prices.
Rot and blocked roads cut the only monsoon supply.
Damping-off and delayed transplanting of early crops.

pests.name: Diamondback moth
pests.impact: Key pest of all crucifers; resistant to many insecticides.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.impact: Colonies on leaves and curds; lower grade.

pests.name: Black rot
pests.impact: V-shaped yellow lesions; spreads in warm, wet weather.

pests.name: Club root
pests.impact: Problem in acidic hill soils (Nilgiris, Darjeeling).

postharvest.respiration: Non-climacteric, high respiration rate. Very sensitive to ethylene: leaves yellow and drop, curds discolour.

loss.detail: Not reported separately; cabbage, a close relative, was 8.15%.

practices: Harvested with a few wrapper leaves to protect the curd.
Do not ship or store with tomatoes, bananas, mangoes or apples (ethylene).
Hydro- or room-cooling quickly after harvest extends life several days.
Sold per piece at retail; trimming removes 40–50% of harvested weight.

steps.what: Cut when curds are compact; packed with leaves in jute bags or crates.
Same-day auction; traders consolidate truckloads for cities.
Azadpur, Kolkata, Patna, Ranchi; hill produce via Solan and Kullu.
Priced per piece by vendors; per piece or per 400–500 g on quick commerce.

supply_chain.packaging: Jute bags or crates with wrapper leaves.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Pusa Meghna, Pusa Kartik Sankar, Pusa Early Synthetic
Pusa Sharad, Pusa Hybrid-2, Pusa Paushja
Pusa Snowball-1, Pusa Snowball K-1, Pusa Snowball Hybrid-1
varieties.note: Late snowball group, also the hill summer crop.

varieties.name: Private hybrids
varieties.note: Widely used for uniform white curds.

policy.what: No MSP or buffer; occasional state market intervention when winter prices collapse.

history.what: Farm prices of ₹1–4 per piece; some farmers plough the crop back in.
Hill-only supply; retail often ₹60–100 per kg equivalent.

signals: Hill arrivals at Solan and weather in Himachal (Jun–Sep).
Plains nursery and transplanting conditions (Jul–Sep rainfall).
Temperature anomalies in Oct–Nov (early curd quality) and Feb (late crop).
business: The monsoon window is the margin window: hill sourcing plus cold chain into plains cities.
Pre-cut florets sell at 4–5 times the whole-head price per kg on quick commerce (see the price snapshot).
Keep cauliflower out of mixed ethylene loads; it is one of the most ethylene-sensitive vegetables.
